chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Does the believer know the one who visits his grave?' He said, 'Yes, and he does not cease to derive comfort with him for as long as he is by his grave. So when he arises and leaves from his grave, loneliness enters into him from his leaving from his grave.'
ai.seo_question: Does the deceased feel lonely after visitors leave the grave?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the psychological and spiritual bond between the living and the deceased in the realm of Barzakh, emphasizing that the comfort derived from visitation is mutual. It underscores the practical Shia tradition of Ziyarat not merely as a ritual for the dead, but as a source of ongoing spiritual solace for the believer, reflecting the belief that the soul remains connected to the physical world through memory and presence.
